sentences.text: Kim Jong-il -LRB- , -LSB- kim.dzʌŋ.il -RSB- or -LSB- kim -RSB- -LSB- tsʌŋ.il -RSB- 16 February 1941/1942 -- 17 December 2011 -RRB- was the supreme leader of the Democratic People 's Republic of Korea -LRB- DPRK -RRB- , commonly referred to as North Korea , from 1994 to 2011 .	supreme leader	List of leaders of North Korea
By the early 1980s Kim had become the heir apparent for the leadership of the country and assumed important posts in the party and army organs .	heir apparent	heir apparent
He succeeded his father and founder of the DPRK , Kim Il-sung , following the elder Kim 's death in 1994 .	Kim Il-sung	Kim Il-sung

Kim Jong-il was the General Secretary of the Workers ' Party of Korea -LRB- WPK -RRB- , Politburo Standing Committee member of WPK , Chairman of the National Defence Commission -LRB- NDC -RRB- of North Korea , and the Supreme Commander of the Korean People 's Army -LRB- KPA -RRB- , the fourth-largest standing army in the world .	General Secretary	General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea	Politburo Standing Committee	Politburo Standing Committee of the Workers' Party of Korea	National Defence Commission	National Defence Commission	Supreme Commander	Supreme Commander of the Korean People's Army	Politburo Standing Committee member	Politburo Standing Committee of the Workers' Party of Korea	Chairman	Chairman of the National Defence Commission of North Korea	fourth-largest standing army	List of countries by number of troops
Kim 's leadership is thought to have been even more authoritarian than his father 's .
During Kim 's regime , the country suffered from famine , partially due to economic mismanagement , and had a poor human rights record .
Kim involved his country in state terrorism and strengthened the role of the military by his Songun , or `` military-first '' , politics .	state terrorism	state terrorism	Songun	Songun
Kim 's rule also saw tentative economic reforms , including the opening of the Kaesong Industrial Park in 2003 .	Kaesong Industrial Park	Kaesong Industrial Park

In April 2009 , North Korea 's constitution was amended to officially refer to him -LRB- and his later successors -RRB- as the `` supreme leader of the DPRK '' .	supreme leader	List of leaders of North Korea

The most common colloquial title given to him during his reign was `` The Dear Leader '' to distinguish him from his father Kim Il-sung , `` The Great Leader '' .	Kim Il-sung	Kim Il-sung	title given to him	List of Kim Jong-il's titles
Following Kim 's failure to appear at important public events in 2008 , foreign observers assumed that Kim had either fallen seriously ill or died .

On 19 December 2011 , the North Korean government announced that he had died two days earlier , whereupon his third son , Kim Jong-un , was promoted to a senior position in the ruling WPK and succeeded him .	Kim Jong-un	Kim Jong-un	had died	Death and state funeral of Kim Jong-il

After his death , he was designated as the `` Eternal General Secretary '' of the WPK and the `` Eternal Chairman of the National Defence Commission '' , in keeping with the tradition of establishing eternal posts for the dead members of the Kim dynasty .
